category_title: Students with ASD exhibiting out-of-seat and assaultive behavior for attention
minimal_context: Brian and his teacher are reviewing his printed behavior contract on Monday morning to agree on his daily targets.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Good morning Brian. Let's look at your printed behavior contract and agree on the targets for today. You need to work successfully through five academic programs before you can access the computer for 30 minutes.

STUDENT: I want to select my own reinforcers.

TUTOR: What do you think you should choose?

STUDENT: I want the computer. I made the wrong choices last week.

TUTOR: Okay, let's start the first academic program.

STUDENT: (Leaves his table without permission and hits the teacher) I don't want to do the programs!

options.A: Preview key vocabulary and concepts covered in the academic programs to familiarize the student with the next day's tasks.
options.B: Review the printed behavior contract with the student, outline the expectations and rewards, and require him to sign it with the teacher.
options.C: Rotate the teacher-student assignment on a daily or weekly basis during the academic programs throughout the regular school week.
options.D: Decrease the academic program work requirements to emphasize accuracy over quantity when the student is completing his daily tasks.
